findings.summary: Clean designed no-op at 17:18:53Z (intel-loop mid-flight). Recorded here mainly as the durable transcription of the supervisor's FULL decision ladder, which is richer than the other lanes' and is otherwise only visible by reading workflow source: (1) active-run dedupe; (2) no-prior-run bootstrap dispatch from accepted state; (3) infra-signature-gated recovery — a failed/cancelled/timed_out latest run is re-dispatched ONLY if its log matches an explicit infrastructure regex list ('runner has received a shutdown signal', 'lost communication with the runner', SPIDER_TRANSIENT_OX_EXHAUSTED, OpenCode/Ox network errors, ECONNRESET/EAI_AGAIN/ENETUNREACH/ENOTFOUND/ETIMEDOUT, service unavailable/bad gateway/gateway timeout); real failures are never auto-recovered ('supervisor will not hide a real failure'); (4) audit-gate integration: REVISE on cycle/intel/<id>/audit triggers same-cycle repair dispatch with repair_from_run_id + declared-inputs-only note ('intel-loop has no human_note input'); BLOCKED stops auto-recovery; (5) continue-flag gate on state/intel_loop.json before any fresh cycle.

Prior art for CF-30 (attribution/receipts): this supervisor reads the persisted audit gate from the cycle branch BEFORE deciding — i.e. it consumes machine-readable receipts rather than run-history heuristics for the REVISE/BLOCKED branches of its policy. Noted so future receipt-extension work starts from this pattern.
